name: The Shoemaker's Children Go Barefoot
description: Breaking into the heavily guarded Fatui facility was unexpectedly easy...
chapter: East of the Moon, West of the Sun

steps.description: Look for a way to exit the room
Look for the owner of the lost item
Look for clues inside the dormitory
Look for clues in the archives
Use the destruction module to reach the upper floor
Go to the second floor of the disposal workshop
Move the cleaning bot to a suitable location
Find a way to open the gate
Find a way to rescue the girl
Use the destruction module to defeat opponents
Enter and explore the Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau
Find a way to enter an empowered state

dialogs.content: #Quick, {NICKNAME}, scooch over a bit and make some room for Paimon...
Wah! Wh—What are you doing!?
H—Huhh?
For some reason, the container seems to already be occupied. It is also clear that the current occupant is most displeased to have uninvited guests...
#Ow-ow-ow! {NICKNAME}, are you okay?
...What the— what hole did you all crawl out from!?
Look, isn't that the thief we're looking for?
...Give it back! Y—You... That's my treasure! Give it back!
Wh—What treasure? We didn't touch anything... We haven't even opened the last chest.
Do you take us for fools? Putting on this "uneven spoils split" act in front of us...
We'll take them all in — both her and her accomplices.
Huh? W—Wait! We don't even know her!
I'm here on a Harbinger's orders.
Pick a more convincing lie, would you?
That still makes you a trespasser. And we arrest those too!
I was passing by and saw the chests...
After some effort, you convince the Fatui guard to go "take a break" elsewhere...
Just lock her up here? Is that what we're doing?
Yep. Poruchik Raskolnikov's orders.
...Did you say "Raskolnikov"?
That's "Poruchik Raskolnikov" to you, thief. Show some respect.
Forget about her. Where's the chest? Have you delivered it to the <color=#00E1FFFF>archives</color>?
Oh, Bakunin's on leave today. I bet he's downing another cup at The Flagship right now.
He sure knows how to enjoy life... Let's leave the chest in the <color=#00E1FFFF>dormitory</color> for now and worry about it tomorrow.
Nice. Now we can return the stuff we took from you by mistake earlier.
I didn't expect it to go so smoothly... I even got something as powerful as the Moonstriders. I'm sure they'll come in handy later.
Speaking of, you aren't bad at all. Maybe just a bit shy of Reed Miller's level, even though we look the same age... And is that a chatty fae next to you?
#Paimon's not fae! Paimon's Paimon, {NICKNAME}'s companion and guide.
Also, why do you keep comparing us to some thief? We're properly registered adventurers!
Eh? Were you commissioned by the Adventurers' Guild to come here, then? Hmm, so you weren't... Makes sense, she did say she only told me.
Well, this isn't exactly a commission from the Adventurers' Guild... Also, why are you getting so nosy? You haven't even told us your name, that's not fair at all.
Name? Call me Netochka. Soon enough though, I'll be known as the reincarnation of the legendary thief Reed Miller, heir to the Great Treasure — Netochka, the Thief Extraordinaire! Hehe.
I think "Honorary Knight" sounds better.
Thief Extraordinaire is cool and all, but "Honorary Knight" just has that righteous ring to it. And... it makes Paimon happy to think about the old friends who use this title!
Anyway... You're not here for a commission, and you don't like Reed Miller, so why are you interested in the Proof of the Cognoscenti?
...Ahh, is this about the Great Treasure? No romance or destiny involved, just here for the loot?
My destiny does not lie here.
What about you then? Aren't you here for the treasure?
Heh heh, well, I must say...
"I kindly ask you to return the Sampo Mill, and all other ill-gotten gains stolen from the Frostmoon Scions, right this instant!"
"Remember, Nod-Krai is our Elysium, and we need neither gods nor pompous lords here!"
Wow, what are you doing?
Haven't you read "The Legends of Reed Miller, Thief Extraordinaire"? *sigh* Never mind. Of course you haven't. I mean, who wouldn't fall for him after reading that?
I came across this book when I was still in Novokitezhgrad... From that moment on, I knew my mission.
Upon my arrival in Nasha Town, the very first person I met gave me a clue regarding the Proof of the Cognoscenti — that's destiny for sure!
Just as the oppressive, greedy governor here stole treasures from the Frostmoon Scions all those years ago, the Fatui now have seized things that don't belong to them.
I must retrieve the Proof of the Cognoscenti from them and find Reed Miller's Great Treasure, so that his name, now forgotten, will be held in esteem once more throughout the world!
Uh...
Um...
Th—There's nothing wrong with that!
And just like how Reed Miller had his trusty companions Shadow Weasel and Wagtail, your unexpected arrival must also be fate.
Otherwise, I'd probably still be stuck there, even if you hadn't taken my treasure.
Hmm? So what exactly is this treasure you're talking about?
It's a thief's starter kit that someone sold me at a "heartbreaking discount." However, none of the doors here have keyholes, so it's completely useless.
That person was like a prophet from the old tales. She seemed to know everything about me and my intentions at first glance...
Not only did she prepare everything I needed, but she also pointed the way forward for me... just for me.
Even Paimon wouldn't fall for that...
What do you mean "Even Paimon wouldn't fall for that"!? But you're right. All that "heartbreaking discount" and exclusive information stuff sounds like a scam...
Wait a minute, did you get all your intel from her? That's not reliable info at all!
That can't be... She was so sincere, there's no way she was lying! Hmm... You just haven't met her yet, I think. When we get back to Nasha Town, I'll introduce you.
As for Raskolnikov... Well, Poruchik Raskolnikov, I do know him. We knew each other back in Novokitezhgrad.
...But never mind him for now. We just need to find the Proof of the Cognoscenti...
So let's get moving! Hehe, it's like we're Reed Miller the Thief Extraordinaire and his two sidekicks, Shadow Weasel and Wagtail, come again.
I call dibs on Shadow Weasel.
So that makes Paimon Wagtail? Wait... Why can't Paimon be Reed Miller?
Character assignments require careful consideration! Naturally, it's first come, first served. And since I was here first, I get to be Reed Miller.
...Ugh, what kind of roleplay is this anyway!?
...*cough* You're right, it is quite juvenile. Then let's go with Netochka the Thief Extraordinaire and her Merry Companions, Goldfinch and Snowy Owl!
Can't I just use my real name?
But I think Goldfinch suits you perfectly! And Snowy Owl really suits Paimon too!
Hmm... Snowy Owl sounds... kinda cool? It's all mysterious and wise and stuff!
Hehe, so that's settled then?
Now we can focus on finding the Proof of the Cognoscenti. Earlier, I heard that the chest was sent to the <color=#00E1FFFF>dormitory</color>.
Those two Fatui didn't follow Raskolnikov's orders. They're definitely in for big trouble. He's always been a meticulous guy. Everything has to go exactly as he plans...
You could call him a perfectionist. No matter what trouble comes up, he always manages to handle it methodically. Some people really admire that trait.
...Anyway, enough about that now. We've got that Proof to find... and I still remember the direction those two Fatui went. Follow me.
Yay, codenames!
#You think that's better, {NICKNAME}? Alright then. Hmm... Snowy Owl doesn't sound too bad. It's all mysterious and wise and stuff!
You can be Shadow Weasel, Paimon.
Eh? No way! Wagtail clearly suits Paimon better. Wait... Why can't Paimon be Reed Miller?
Character assignments require careful consideration! Naturally, it's first come, first served. And since I was here first, I get to be Reed Miller.
Then I'll be Reed Miller.
No way! I was here first, so I should be the one playing Reed Miller.
Paimon is the most unique character amongst us, so it makes perfect sense for her to play Reed Miller!
So you're a die-hard Reed Miller fan.
I'm a practical person.
I'm the hero who saved the city from the evil dragon.
Well, I've heard stories like that, though they sound more like things children would enjoy?
My title would leave you quaking in your boots.
Oh! I get it, you're just trying to act tough. It's fine to be a nobody, as long as you make something of yourself later, like me!
There's nothing here — but how... Did you find anything on your end?
Looks like a journal. Pretty careless of them to leave it out in the open like this.
Everything should be fine now, let's go!
Then I'll be off! Don't fall too far behind!
Phew! Finally, we're safe... at least for now?
Ugh, just our rotten luck! Paimon never would've guessed that the container... y'know, contained a thief the Fatui were chasing!
We wouldn't be in such a mess if it weren't for her. Great, now the chest is gone, and we had to fight the Fatui...
Oh and, and! She even accused us of taking some treasure of hers. Lies! Lies and slander! Ugh, the more Paimon thinks about it—!
Speaking of...
...What's this?
Something I swiped in the dark just now.
Is this the treasure she mentioned? Uh, what should we do now?
Let's take it to the lost and found.
Yeah... wait no! We don't even know if there is one around here, and, even if there were, it's not like we can just waltz in there, much less her!
Hmm... Paimon wouldn't have cared as much if it were just an item from a chest no one owns...
We should find a way to return it... A—As long as it's returned to its rightful owner, everything will be fine!
But we've probably already caught the attention of the Fatui here, so a little extra caution could save us a lot of trouble!
Let's just leave it here and pretend we didn't see anything.
Mm-hmm, maybe she'll come back and look for it... but will she really?
Sorry, I made trouble for you again...
We're used to it at this point. Now, if you ditched us or tried to shoo us off at this point... Now that would make us mad!
...Okay. Then, thank you, for keeping me company.
That's more like it! Speaking of, didn't that Ras guy say he'd meet us at the highest point? Why's the lift malfunctioning, then?
What should we do? Do we try to fix it?
Knocking on it a few times might do the trick.
I doubt it's that easy to fix!
Th—That scared Paimon! She thought it'd hit her for sure...
Now we can jump up.
Oh! True, we did something similar when we collected data for Fanngel. But, what about Netochka...?
Hm? You knew about this strange lightning, too? A treasure hunter I met told me that jumping from where the lightning strikes to the top level should be a cinch with the Moonstriders.
Should we go now?
I need to do some prep first...
Then I'll wait for you.
The Moonstriders are our best shot.
Um... I don't think they'll manage that far up. If we had some other help, though...
You two...! If it hadn't been you, I'd have snagged the Proof of the Cognoscenti and gotten away by now! And... you also stole my—
Woah, calm down! Things were chaotic back then and we didn't mean to take anything from you. And see? We're here to return it to its rightful owner.
A—Anyway, we'll return it to you right now... Uh, how should we do that?
Could you open the door?
She probably can't... Maybe we should just leave it here...
...You can't be serious. What is this cold indifference you're showing to a fair damsel in distress!? If it were Reed Miller, he would have rescued me in a heartbeat.
...Fair damsel?
A—Am I not one?
Hmm... You're also here for the Proof of the Cognoscenti, right? How about this — you help me get out of here, and I'll consider sharing some clues with you.
I think we'll do just fine without your clues.
That's right. We can find our own way! We're very experienced in that department.
Huh? W—Wait, don't go! Then, how... how about information on Raskolnikov? Poruchik Raskolnikov. They say he's quite somebody here.
Though wreaking havoc here wouldn't be a bad play... It'd be just like how Reed Miller ransacked the governor's palace, took back the Sampo Mill, and stole the heart of the governor's daughter...
...Ahem! Anyway, I—I mean, it would be in your interest to claim your treasure with grace, no? The information I have will definitely help!
P—Please, I beg you, please help me! If Raskolnikov learns that I'm here... I...
#What do you say, {NICKNAME}? Should we help her?
We're already here, may as well.
Hah! Splendid! Today really is my lucky day! Now, I've already swiped an ID card off the guards earlier, so I just need the other one, and we'll be set!
I don't know where the other card is... but even if you find it, there's still the problem of <color=#00E1FFFF>getting it inside and placing it high up</color> to remove the barrier.
I guess we can do it for the intel...
My name is not Reed Miller.
Of course you're not, hmph. No one in our time is his equal.
Since you can see us, we'll just leave it here.
Almost there... I need to make some final preparations. Hmm, "Goldfinch," if you're ready, let's go.
Whoa, a floor plan! Did we really just get our hands on some top-secret info this easily?
Paimon thought grabbing an important item like this would come with some kind of dramatic scene...
(A few thick volumes...)
(The section about the Nothing Passage seems quite intriguing...)
(No usable information can be discerned...)

Say, the good ol' Poruchik collecting the <color=#00E1FFFF>Proof of the Cognoscenti</color>... Think that counts as an abuse of power for personal gain? I mean, we're here on a mission. The heck are we doing, digging holes for him like moles...
What happens up there is none of our business.
Do you think reporting it to the higher-ups will do anything?
'Cause it seems to me that they don't like <color=#00E1FFFF>Poruchik Raskolnikov</color> up there either. Maybe my report's just the opportunity they'll need!
You should keep these words to yourself.
Huh? What, are you trying to get ahead of me? That's low of you, real low!
*sigh*...
Hmm? Paimon can see something from here...
Looks like the disposal workshop. It's on the floor plan too. I guess this is where they get rid of defective products.
Look up, I think I see someone...
(Zoom in on the scene.)
It's Raskolnikov! And the chest!
"Sir, the Proof of the Cognoscenti has been recovered."
"Good work, you've done well. Rest up before the next assignment. Ah, and let's have Nod-Krai Hot Dogs for dinner tonight."
...Wait. Why did Paimon get so caught up in acting?
Looks like you're both masters of disguise and infiltration, Goldfinch, Snowy Owl. You sure are reliable partners.
However, it would be better if you both were more committed to playing the characters, in terms of speech and mannerisms...
Huh!? What are you, a film director? That's asking way too much!
Huh? This is nothing compared to what's required of ballet performers!
So you watch ballet? Paimon thought you only watched... Wait, that's not the point here!
Anyway, let's put the roleplay aside for now. We can pretty much confirm that the guy called Ras... Ras-whatever, has retrieved the Proof of the Cognoscenti, right?
By the way, why are the Fatui collecting the Proof? Are they also interested in the Great Treasure? ...C—Could they be in the middle of a financial crisis!?
That's what happens when you spend money recklessly.
Hmm... It's hard to imagine that the Fatui would take interest in the Great Treasure because they're out of funds...
Is this that Ras guy's personal interest, then? Wow, asking his subordinates to find treasure for him, that's...
Despicable!
What do they call this again... Yes, that's it!— an "abuse of power"! Truly despicable!
Um... If it's the Raskolnikov I know, he wouldn't do this out of personal interest. In fact, he doesn't have anything that could even be considered a "personal interest."
There must be some motive... The only thing he's interested in is getting ahead of the game, so maybe he plans to bribe his superior using the Great Treasure...
Come to think of it, Paimon never asked... What exactly is your relationship with that guy, Netochka? It's unusual for a thief to know so much about a Fatui officer.
...W—We just knew each other from before. We're both from Novokitezhgrad, so it's not that strange that we know each other, right?
Besides, think about it — no one ever questioned why the fae governor in the story wanted to seize the Sampo Mill, right?
Point is, the mill didn't belong to him, just like how the Proof of the Cognoscenti doesn't belong to the Fatui. So naturally, we — the ones on the side of justice — must take it back.
Goldfinch, Snowy Owl, this is where we carve our names in fame and glory as Reed Miller's successors!
For fame and glory!
#Well, if {NICKNAME}... if Goldfinch says so!
But that guy is also an officer here, right? How are we supposed to get the Proof from him without exposing ourselves...?
Hmm... Based on the floor plan, we can quickly get to the second floor of the disposal workshop from the archives, and get it done before he leaves.
He thinks everything is under his control, including the chest, which ended up in his hands just as he wanted. But he can't control us...
Hehe, that'll be so Reed Miller! Appearing at unexpected times and places, making a dashing entrance, then gracefully departing... A perfect performance.
For the Great Treasure!
Living the dream!
Ugh, yeah! Reaping the fruits of other people's labor while lounging on a comfy chair...
Doesn't sound very likely...
You're right... Building a huge structure here and deploying so many people doesn't sound like financial crisis to Paimon at all.
"I brought the goods. What about you?"
"What's the rush? Are you telling me how to do my job?"
"Hmm, this is indeed what we agreed upon. As for what we brought, if you want to inspect them... come right this way."
Huh? How did we end up on the other side? We followed the floor plan exactly.
Do ants in a maze know that they travel along pre-designed paths? I am surprised that you took the bait without a speck of doubt.
You've fallen right into my trap, little thief.
Raskolnikov...
It's Poruchik Raskolnikov. It's been a while, Netochka. I never expected Police Chief Stalanov's daughter to end up playing thief in this godforsaken place.
...Police Chief's daughter?
It seems these two playmates in your game of house don't know you very well. Not that it matters.
I must say, your little farce helped me root out quite a few deceptive, two-faced subordinates.
Organization members who fail to execute orders to the letter should be terminated, immediately.
Never mind Netochka's background. We've met lots of odd ducks — so what if she's the police chief's daughter?
Snowy Owl...
And all that talk about executing orders to the letter... You're all just moving a chest back and forth! The one giving nonsensical orders is the real weirdo here.
Such a terrible waste of manpower...
Oh, right! All this nonsense almost made Paimon forget that — that's what's important here!
And it doesn't belong to the Fatui. I must take it back — that's my mission!
Take it back? Ridiculous. Of course Reed Miller's treasure doesn't belong to the Fatui — it belongs to Her Majesty the Tsaritsa.
Whoever brings the Great Treasure back to Snezhnograd will be rewarded. Should I do so, I could even be promoted to staff officer.
I knew it. You're as obsessed with these titles as ever.
...Enough! Since you claim to be Reed Miller's successor, you must be prepared to follow in his footsteps too.
This place shall be your execution ground. If you have any last words, now is the time.
But I will not relay them to Chief Stalanov on your behalf. It's best that he never finds out what happened to his precious daughter. I owe my former teacher this much respect.
Precious daughter? Feh. All he ever cares about are his endless cases and "promising juniors" like you!
...Hah, you're no better. Still as arrogant as ever.
But it matters little, because this will all end shortly.
Ugh...
So, you really don't know who I am?
So long as you're an accomplice of the thief illegally infiltrating the Experimental Design Bureau, this place will be your grave too.
Looks like we'll have to do this the hard way...
I'm sorry, I lied to you. I do know him, but none of what I know will help us. I can't even help much in battle...
#There's no point saying that now, Netochka. Just leave the fighting to us... to {NICKNAME}!
I knew it would end up like this...
But you prefer things this way, right? Straight-up fights are better than wild chest hunts... Whoa, watch out!
Mere Fatui joiners...
Hand over the Proof of the Cognoscenti.
Never mind that now, let's find a place to hide before we get caught!
What!? How...
Oh! Paimon knows! This is what they call "Turning their own blade unto them"!
...It seems I've miscalculated. The Proof of the Cognoscenti that you seek is in my hands. If you want it, follow me outside!
I'll be waiting for you at the highest point of the Experimental Design Bureau.
Eh!? He ran away? That... that coward!
Leave it to me! I'll go after him!
F—Finally made it up here...
He's alone? Paimon thought he ran so fast because he was going to call for reinforcements.
An ambush, perhaps...?
Ah! How despicable!
I'll... I'll fight with you!
If you want the Proof of the Cognoscenti, you must defeat me first! That is, if you can.
Then he will have to pay the price for his arrogance.
Looking down on us... We'll show him!
Phew... We won. Now, hand the Proof over.
...Come and get it yourself.
Paimon didn't expect you to admit defeat so easily... And there really weren't any reinforcements!
This is good.
It sure saves a lot of trouble, but this isn't what usually happens. If this is a trap...
Didn't you say you'd get promoted if you brought the Great Treasure back to Snezhnograd? Why are you giving us the Proof so easily?
When did I ever say that I would be the one to do that? Keeping the Proof at the Design Bureau will bring nothing but trouble.
As long as it stays here, there will be an endless swarm of rats coveting it, trying to infiltrate this supposedly impregnable stronghold, just like you lot.
I am to guard the Design Bureau and ensure its efficient operation. But orders from my superiors must be obeyed.
This already constitutes insubordination, of course... but due to my failings, the Proof of the Cognoscenti that we spent so much manpower to find was ultimately stolen by a petty thief.
Now you can go back to Nasha Town... or wherever you want, to announce your victory.
...Did you lose to us on purpose?
Losing to an opponent who has deep ties with the Harbingers brings no shame upon me. I'm impressed you managed to find such help...
So you did know about us.
Eh!? I knew that you were exceptionally skilled, Goldfinch, but...
...Haha! A fool blessed with blind luck. I've always hated your kind...
Forget it. Take the Proof of the Cognoscenti. The Experimental Design Bureau will no longer devote manpower to searching for this accursed thing. We won't meet again.
But if you insist on future unwelcome visitation, I'll show you what I'm really made of.
Raskolnikov leaves...
This curtain call is completely different from what I imagined, even with the Proof of the Cognoscenti...
I need some time to think about all this...
Things going so smoothly makes me uneasy...
C—Could this be the trigger for an even bigger trap!?
If only he were the big bad governor oppressing the innocent, then I would have... Now, I'm made to look like the unreasonable child...
*sigh* I'm sorry for dragging you into this farce. Say, do you really have connections to the Harbingers? That's... a surprise. If you'd told me earlier...
#We could have been called "{NICKNAME} the Thief Extraordinaire and {M#His}{F#Her} Merry Companions" or "Paimon the Thief Extraordinaire and Her Merry Companions"... or something similar? Haha...
Right, speaking of which, you should take the Proof of the Cognoscenti. Yes, it's much better in your hands than mine.
Why do you sound so defeated all of a sudden?
Yeah, why are you giving up already? And, didn't something like this happen just a moment ago?
You and that Ras-whatever guy, you talk in circles around each other and act like everything's settled afterwards.
And that makes Paimon feel kinda uneasy, even if we did get the Proof! It's like a sneeze that just won't come out...
I just... suddenly realized that, compared to Raskolnikov and all of you, I'm just an insignificant character in the story, like I've always been...
I wish I could become Reed Miller, a true protagonist with an adventure to call my own — someone who can claim the spotlight and receive the adoration of all...
So I told myself that it was my destiny to become Reed Miller's successor. To turn my fantasy into reality, I came here in search of clues about the Great Treasure.
Back in Nasha Town, Hidimbi gave me some clues on the Proof of the Cognoscenti and said I was special, that she had chosen me. I was so happy at the time...
But now that I think about it, how could I possibly have been the only one? She must have had other motives.
All that talk about being Reed Miller's successor, about destiny and mission... they were never meant for me. I'm still just a pebble by the roadside, worthless and unnoticed...
You write your own story.
Yeah, how does that saying go... "Everyone's the protagonist of their own story"?
So what's wrong with us being "Netochka the Thief Extraordinaire and Her Merry Companions" in your story?
Ah, but like we agreed, Snowy Owl is the character who embodies wisdom and beauty, and who's just the slightest bit mysterious! It's a role made for Paimon, hehe.
#As for {NICKNAME}... Sorry, Goldfinch, {M#he}{F#she} can be the {M#handsome}{F#beautiful} and cool character!
I envy you, Paimon... I wish I could think that way. Do you have any tips on finding happiness?
#Hmm... Well, Paimon's happy just being with {NICKNAME}.
#Whether it's eating Chicken-Mushroom Skewers in the wild or feasting in a fancy restaurant, it's all good as long as it's done with {NICKNAME}!
#So if I want to be happy like you, Paimon, I'd need a companion like {NICKNAME}...
Hmm... That doesn't sound right. Why do you always have to imitate others, Netochka?
You just have to be yourself. Everyone has a chance of becoming Reed Miller's successor, but only you can be you.
But if I'm just being myself... would I actually deserve it? To be a brilliant character in people's eyes, or a special someone?
Hey, why are you still going on about this? It doesn't matter what others think!
Paimon doesn't get why you keep worrying over it. Even if you're not someone's "special someone" or a big name, you can still be happy!
So you think none of that matters... That's really broad-minded, Paimon...
...Broad-minded? Hmm, yeah, that's right! That's the secret to happiness! Hehe, Paimon can drop insightful lines too.
#Well, since you think none of that matters, then... {NICKNAME}, would you become my best companion? I don't expect to be your special someone, but...
W—Wait a minute! B—Best companion? That won't do!
#That title belongs to Paimon, r—right? {NICKNAME}?
Haha, you talk the talk but can't walk the walk, Paimon!
Hmm? Netochka, you... Are you making fun of Paimon!?
Since you're already feeling well enough to joke around... Hmph, and here Paimon was, just a bit, a tiiiny bit, worried about you.
Quick, say thank you to Paimon.
#Mm! Thank you, Paimon, and thank you too, {NICKNAME}. Snowy Owl, Goldfinch, you're both my dear companions!
By the way, what are your plans after this? And, the Proof of the Cognoscenti...
I'll let you take the Proof this time. You've earned it. But if we cross paths elsewhere in the future, don't expect any mercy from me, alright?
Oh? So we'll be rivals next time we meet? Hehe, the two of us are formidable rivals to have, y'know!
It's a shame we can't become best companions, but I'll work hard to become your greatest rival instead. Just you wait and see!
Don't overthink it. Do what makes you happy.
Paimon doesn't get it. Rather than thinking about things like fate or destiny... isn't it better to live happily?
They're all empty! This is the only one left...
We've looked up and down and haven't seen hide or hair of that thief. Where in the world could she be hiding...?
Maybe she's gotten what she wanted and already made the big escape?
Haha. That's not gonna look good on our monthly reports, let me tell you... or Poruchik Raskolnikov's...
Someone's approaching. Let's hide! Um, <color=#00E1FFFF>that container</color> looks like a good spot...
(A container that is just here for some reason.)
(Reminds me of the time Netochka, red as a beet, pushing us out during our previous attempt at hiding inside one...)
(There's clearly no chest on the bed, so maybe under it... Whoa, no chest in sight, and completely spotless, to boot...)
Hey! Where do you think you're going?
Oh, you weasel! Trying to ditch us!
S—Say what you want! A true master thief only has her eyes on the treasure. I couldn't care less about anything else!
...That way, hurry!
...Got... Stay put...
Netochka... Are you sure it's this way? It looks dangerous...
Trust me, this is definitely the right way. Besides, isn't sneaking across rooftops what cool rogues do? Ahem... We need to keep our voices down.
Don't worry, Snowy Owl. I'm here with you. Let's go!
(I'll leave the one on the right to you, Goldfinch!)
(Oh, I didn't expect the Moonstriders to come in handy so soon. I'll take care of the top, watch this!)
Piece of cake! Are you all okay?
